input.rationale: The effects-of-termination clause (paragraph 4(c)) addresses only cessation of the Services, revocation of the licence, and each Party's return or destruction of the other's Confidential Information. There is no transition-assistance obligation, no obligation to return or export our data (Content, Requests, reporting and visitor data held by Kubient) in a usable format, and no deletion certification; nothing elsewhere in the Agreement supplies these. That fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus a 30-day export), and the current "return or destroy" election lets Kubient unilaterally destroy our data on termination, which is walk-away territory. We therefore insert the preferred transition, machine-readable return within 30 days, and certified deletion language into paragraph 4(c).

proposal.summary: Insert transition-assistance and Customer Data return/deletion-certification obligation into the effects-of-termination clause (paragraph 4(c)).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Paragraph 4(c) only requires the parties to return or destroy Confidential Information, so we have added an orderly exit: up to six months of transition assistance at Kubient's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance with the same thirty-day export.

ops.text: Notwithstanding subsection (iv), Kubient shall (A) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Kubient's then-current rates; (B) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Customer, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all Content, Requests, reporting and other data of, or collected for or on behalf of, Customer that is in Kubient's possession or control ("Customer Data"); and (C) thereafter delete all Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.
